texts.preamble: Padam Singh vs The State Of M.P. on 22 May, 2017 Author: Atul Sreedharan Bench: Atul Sreedharan Criminal Revision No. 605/2000. (1) High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat At Jabalpur Criminal Revision No. 605/2000. Padam Singh. Versus The State of M.P. ********* Shri Rudra Dev Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner. Shri Arvind Singh, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent- State. ********* Order
texts.facts: He has submitted that Criminal Revision No. 605/2000. material on record put into grave doubt, whether such a right of the petitioner had been fulfilled by the prosecution. 3. The brief facts essential to appreciate the case against the petitioner is that a complaint was instituted by the complainant K.L. Jaiswal Food Inspector, in which it was stated that on 28/08/1993 at about 9 O'clock, the complainant had gone to bus stand, Obedullaganj to check the quality of food material. The petitioner herein said to have found carrying 2 Kgs. of mixed milk. On doubt that the petitioner may carry adulterated milk, the complainant introduced himself and Padam Singh vs The State Of M.P. on 22 May, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105590948/ 1 insisted to take the sample of the said milk. A notice form-6 was given to the petitioner and upon the consent of the petitioner 750ml milk was purchased as sample. After following due procedure, the milk was sent to the Public Analyst and the report of public analyst revealed that the milk was adulterated. The complaint was filed by the Food Inspector as mentioned hereinabove and the trial court convicted the petitioner for the said offence.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court to paragraph No. 10 of the appellate court's order in which learned counsel for the appellant/ petitioner had placed before the appellate court the judgment of this Court in Food Inspector Balaghat Vs. Tejlal 1995 Cr. L.R. (M.P.) 95 in which this court was pleased to acquit the petitioner in that case, this court arrived at the finding that Criminal Revision No. 605/2000. the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Act was not fulfilled. The Court observed that the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with report of Public Analyst which was alleged to have been sent to the petitioner in that case was not proved, as prosecution failed to place on record either the receipt of the registered post by which the said notice and the report was dispatched or the acknowledgment with the said notice and report were received by the accused. 4. 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has thereafter argued that even before the trial court, consistent stand of the petitioner herein was that he did not receive notice or public analyst report as mandatory under Section 13(2) of the Act.
